title: Three quick questions about sharing work
context: You send emails, reports and files to colleagues and clients every week.

questions.text: You receive an email as a Bcc recipient and select Reply all. Who gets your reply?

options.feedback: Reply all also goes to everyone on To and Cc, who then see you were on Bcc.
options.rightWhen: The Reply button sends only to the sender.

options.text: The sender and everyone on To and Cc
options.feedback: Reply all copies the To and Cc lists, so everyone there sees you were on Bcc.

options.text: Everyone, including the other Bcc recipients
options.feedback: Your email program never gets the other Bcc addresses, so it can't reply to them.
options.rightWhen: Reply all does reach every address you can see.

questions.text: Your team's sales fell 50% in March, then rose 50% in April. How do April's sales compare with February's?

options.feedback: The 50% rise is on March's smaller total, so it wins back only half of the fall.
options.rightWhen: A fall and a rise cancel out when they are the same amount in dollars.

options.feedback: March's sales were half of February's. April's rise added half of March's sales, so April's sales were three quarters of February's, which is 25% lower.
March's sales were half of February's. April's rise added half of March's sales, so April's sales were three quarters of February's.

questions.text: You draw black boxes over a client's account numbers in a PDF, save it and send it. What happens to the numbers under the boxes?

options.text: They stay in the file, and anyone can copy them
options.feedback: A drawn box sits on top of the text. A redaction tool deletes the text.

options.text: They stay in the file, but no one can read them
options.feedback: A drawn box sits on top of the text, where anyone can still copy or search for it.
options.rightWhen: Boxes do hide the numbers on a printed page.

options.text: They stay in the file until you save it
options.feedback: Saving keeps the boxes and the text under them. A redaction tool deletes the text.
options.rightWhen: Saving does make a redaction tool's change permanent.
